messages:
matthew_l: Ran a short microbench for AWQ int8 with interleaved group packing + structured sparsity (2:1). Quick summary: throughput looks +12% vs baseline, median latency stable, but p95/p99 regressed ~8-15% on short chat workloads (seq_len=64). attaching flame + traces.

sara_v: can you paste the exact command and model so I can repro?

matthew_l: command:
```
./bench/run.sh --model llama2-13b --quant awq --group-size 64 --sparsity 0.5 --batch 1 --seq 64 --pack-mode interleaved
```

jin_w: thanks. looked at the perf traces — kernel chooser is falling back to the scalar unpack path for ~50% of layers when sparsity metadata isn't byte-aligned. that fallback kills the vectorized GEMM/pack hotpath. also seeing lots of tiny memcpy spikes from KV cache warmups.

matthew_l: noted. profiler hotspots show `pack_matrix_stride` spending time in `pack_pad_bytes` for group_size=64. alignment rounding + appended sparsity metadata seems to cause extra pad loops.

jin_w: quick experiment: try group-size 32 or 16 and enable `--pack-prefetch=on`. group=32 eliminated the fallback in my local run and recovered p99. also try `--sparsity-format=bytemask` instead of bitset.

sara_v: is this AWQ-specific? we saw something vaguely similar in GPTQ a while back. could be shared.

jin_w: it's more pronounced in AWQ because AWQ interleaves scale/zero per group and the signed-bytes layout plus a bitset sparsity footer shifts the payload alignment. GPTQ packer uses a different layout so less affected.

benchbot: Automated perf summary for run 3051234567-1: group=64,spars=0.5 -> p99=121ms (+14%). group=32,spars=0.5 -> p99=98ms (+2%). Artifacts uploaded: perf_flame.svg, raw_traces.tar.gz.

matthew_l: I opened a bisect PR to isolate the packer change and added verbose packing logs. @sara_v can you run e2e with group=48? curious whether odd group sizes avoid the pad edge case.

sara_v: kicking off group=48 run now, will report in ~20m :hourglass:

jin_w: short-term runtime mitigation: kernel chooser should detect misaligned sparsity metadata and prefer the vectorized unpack when unpack cost > threshold. I'll file an issue and prototype a guard.

matthew_l: created infra ticket INF-872 and attached the perf traces + bisect PR reference. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sara_v: update: group=48 p99=101ms — still worse than 32 but much better than 64. trace: https://artifacts.redwood/3051234567/trace.html

jin_w: good signal. plan: 1) patch packer to force byte-align sparsity footer 2) add kernel-chooser heuristic to avoid scalar fallback 3) canary next week. I'll start the PR.
